Every error Flowdesk shows has a code. The support form attaches the last one automatically.

## Sign-in errors

| code | message | what it means | what to do |

# Flowdesk FAQ

## I can't sign in. What should I check?

Most sign-in problems have one of a handful of causes. Go through them in order:

1. **The error message.** Every sign-in error has a code (for example `AUTH_423_LOCKED`); see
   [Error codes](error-codes.md) for what each one means.
2. **Too many attempts.** After 5 wrong passwords in 15 minutes the account is locked for
   30 minutes. See [Signing in](sign-in.md#account-lockout).
3. **Your organization uses SSO.** If your admin turned on "Require SSO", the email and password
   form no longer works for you: use **Sign in with SSO**. See [Single sign-on](sso.md).
4. **Two-factor codes.** Codes rejected right after the password usually mean the clock on your
   phone is off. See [Two-factor authentication](two-factor.md#codes-are-rejected).
5. **Your organization's subscription.** If an invoice is unpaid for more than 14 days, the
   workspace is suspended and members can't sign in. See [Billing](billing.md#unpaid-invoices).
6. **An invitation link.** Invitations expire after 7 days. See
   [Members and invitations](members-and-invites.md#invitations).
7. **The desktop app.** Check [Known issues](known-issues.md) for your version.

If none of these fits, contact support with the error code and the time you tried.

passages.label: kb/sign-in.md › Signing in › Account lockout
passages.text:
## Account lockout

After **5 failed password attempts within 15 minutes**, the account is locked for
**30 minutes**. While it is locked, every sign-in attempt fails with `AUTH_423_LOCKED`
("Too many attempts. Try again later"), even with the correct password, and does not extend
the lock.

To get back in sooner:

- reset your password with **Forgot password?**: a completed reset unlocks the account at once;
- or ask an admin of your organization to open **Admin › Members**, find you and click
  **Unlock**.

Support can't unlock accounts on the Free and Team plans faster than these two ways.

passages.label: kb/members-and-invites.md › Members and invitations › Changing your email
passages.text:
## Unlocking a member

When a member is locked after too many sign-in attempts, an admin can click **Unlock** next to
their name in **Admin › Members**.

## Changing your email

**Profile › Account › Email**. We send a confirmation link to the new address. In an
organization that requires SSO the email comes from the identity provider and can't be changed
in Flowdesk.

passages.label: kb/sign-in.md › Signing in › Resetting a password
passages.text:
## Passwords

A password needs at least 10 characters. It is checked against lists of leaked passwords;
a rejected password says so. Changing your password signs you out on all other devices.

## Resetting a password

**Forgot password?** on the sign-in page sends a reset link to your email from
`no-reply@flowdesk.app`. The link is valid for **1 hour** and can be used once. If no email
arrives within 10 minutes, check the spam folder, then ask your admin to confirm the email
address on your account.

Resetting your password also **unlocks** an account that was locked after too many attempts.

If your organization requires SSO, there is no Flowdesk password to reset: the reset email
says so and points you to your company's identity provider.

passages.text:
## Require SSO

With **Require SSO** on, members of the organization can only sign in through the identity
provider:

- the email and password form rejects them with `AUTH_403_SSO_REQUIRED` ("Your organization
  requires single sign-on");
- **Sign in with Google** is disabled for them;
- password reset emails no longer contain a reset link;
- owners can still sign in with a password, so a broken SSO configuration never locks everyone
  out.

When an admin turns it on, existing sessions stay valid until they expire; the change shows up
the next time someone signs in.

## Signing in with SSO

On the sign-in page click **Sign in with SSO**, enter your work email (or the organization's
workspace name), and you are sent to your company's identity provider. After signing in there
you come back to Flowdesk.

If the identity provider says you are not assigned to the application, ask your IT team to
assign you to the Flowdesk app in Okta, Entra ID or Google Workspace. Flowdesk support cannot
change assignments in your identity provider.

passages.label: kb/sso.md › Single sign-on (SSO) › Setting up SSO
passages.text:
# Single sign-on (SSO)

Available on the **Business** and **Enterprise** plans. Flowdesk supports SAML 2.0 with Okta,
Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Google Workspace and OneLogin.

## Setting up SSO

An owner opens **Admin › Security › Single sign-on**, adds the identity provider's metadata URL
and verifies the email domain (for example `acme.com`) with a DNS TXT record. Users are created
on first sign-in if "Just-in-time provisioning" is on. Enterprise plans also support SCIM.

passages.text:
# Known issues

Problems we know about, with workarounds. Fixed issues stay listed for 60 days.

## Desktop app for macOS 3.4.0 and 3.4.1: sign-in loop

**Status: fixed in 3.4.2 (released 2026-10-02).**

After signing in through the browser (with Google, SSO or a password), the browser says you are
signed in, but the app shows the sign-in screen again. It happens on macOS 26 because the app
can't save its refresh token in the keychain. The web app is not affected.

Fix: update the app to 3.4.2 or later with **Flowdesk › Check for updates**, or download it from
`flowdesk.app/download`. If the app can't get past the sign-in screen to update, download the
installer from the website and install it over the old version. If the loop continues after
updating, open **Keychain Access**, delete the items named "Flowdesk", and sign in again.

# API and API keys

The REST API lives at `https://api.flowdesk.app/v2`. It is available on the Team plan and above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an API key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer fd_live_3f9a...
```

Keys start with `fd_live_`. Query parameters (`?api_key=`) are not accepted.

cases.question: Why isn't authorization working?
cases.answer:
The issue is likely due to your device's clock being out of sync, which is causing the two-factor authentication code to be invalid. This is a common problem after traveling or manually setting the time on your phone. The error code `AUTH_401_OTP_INVALID` indicates that the code is either wrong or expired, and the clock discrepancy is the most probable cause [2].

To fix this:
1. On your Android phone, turn on automatic date and time settings (**Settings › System › Date & time › Set time automatically**).
2. In Google Authenticator, you can also use **Settings › Time correction for codes › Sync now** to adjust the clock for the authenticator app.
3. Wait for a new code and try signing in again.

If the issue persists, you can use one of your remaining backup codes to sign in.

passages.label: kb/two-factor.md › Two-factor authentication › Codes are rejected
passages.text:
## Codes are rejected

A code is valid for 30 seconds and is computed from the current time, so the clock of the
device running the authenticator app matters. If codes fail with `AUTH_401_OTP_INVALID` even
though you type them correctly, the device's clock is almost always off by more than 30 seconds.
This often happens after travelling, when the time zone or time was set by hand.

To fix it:

1. On the phone, turn on automatic date and time (Android: **Settings › System › Date & time ›
   Set time automatically**; iOS: **Settings › General › Date & Time › Set Automatically**).
2. In Google Authenticator on Android you can also use **Settings › Time correction for codes ›
   Sync now**.
3. Wait for a fresh code and try again.

Until the clock is fixed, a **backup code** gets you in.

passages.text:
## Unpaid invoices

If a payment fails, the subscription becomes **past due** and the owner and billing admins are
emailed. Flowdesk retries the card on days 3, 7 and 14.

- During the first **14 days** past due, everything keeps working.
- After 14 days the workspace is **suspended**: members can't sign in and get
  `AUTH_402_ORG_SUSPENDED` ("Your organization's workspace is suspended"). Integrations and the
  API stop too.
- Owners and billing admins can still sign in, but only to **Admin › Billing**, where they can
  pay the open invoice or change the card. Access returns for everyone within a few minutes of a
  successful payment.
- Data of a suspended workspace is kept for **90 days**, then deleted.

Members can't pay on behalf of the organization; they need to contact their owner or billing
admin.

## I can't sign in. What should I check?

Most sign-in problems have one of a handful of causes. Go through them in order:

1. **The error message.** Every sign-in error has a code (for example `AUTH_423_LOCKED`); see

   workspace is suspended and members can't sign in. See [Billing](billing.md#unpaid-invoices).

   [Members and invitations](members-and-invites.md#invitations).

## Creating and managing keys

Admins and owners create keys in **Admin › API keys › New key**, give them a name and choose
scopes (`tasks:read`, `tasks:write`, `projects:read`, `projects:write`, `members:read`). The
full key is shown once; afterwards only its prefix is visible.

A key belongs to the person who created it and acts with their permissions. A key is
**revoked**:

- when someone revokes it in **Admin › API keys**;
- automatically, when the member who created it is **deactivated** or removed from the
  organization;
- when the organization's workspace is suspended (it works again after payment).

A revoked key can't be restored: create a new key and replace it in your integration. To avoid
breakage when people leave, create integration keys from a dedicated service member.

passages.text:
## Codes are rejected

A code is valid for 30 seconds and is computed from the current time, so the clock of the
device running the authenticator app matters. If codes fail with `AUTH_401_OTP_INVALID` even
though you type them correctly, the device's clock is almost always off by more than 30 seconds.
This often happens after travelling, when the time zone or time was set by hand.

To fix it:

1. On the phone, turn on automatic date and time (Android: **Settings › System › Date & time ›
   Set time automatically**; iOS: **Settings › General › Date & Time › Set Automatically**).
2. In Google Authenticator on Android you can also use **Settings › Time correction for codes ›
   Sync now**.
3. Wait for a fresh code and try again.

Until the clock is fixed, a **backup code** gets you in.

## Invitations

Admins invite people in **Admin › Members › Invite** by email. The invitee gets an email with a
link to create their account. Each invitation needs a free seat.

  password; the invitation still has to be accepted first.
- An invitee can't ask support to activate the account: only the organization's admins can
  invite or resend.

passages.text:
## Signing in with SSO

On the sign-in page click **Sign in with SSO**, enter your work email (or the organization's
workspace name), and you are sent to your company's identity provider. After signing in there
you come back to Flowdesk.

If the identity provider says you are not assigned to the application, ask your IT team to
assign you to the Flowdesk app in Okta, Entra ID or Google Workspace. Flowdesk support cannot
change assignments in your identity provider.

passages.label: kb/sso.md › Single sign-on (SSO) › Require SSO
passages.text:
## Require SSO

With **Require SSO** on, members of the organization can only sign in through the identity
provider:

- the email and password form rejects them with `AUTH_403_SSO_REQUIRED` ("Your organization
  requires single sign-on");
- **Sign in with Google** is disabled for them;
- password reset emails no longer contain a reset link;
- owners can still sign in with a password, so a broken SSO configuration never locks everyone
  out.

When an admin turns it on, existing sessions stay valid until they expire; the change shows up
the next time someone signs in.

passages.text:
# Single sign-on (SSO)

Available on the **Business** and **Enterprise** plans. Flowdesk supports SAML 2.0 with Okta,
Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Google Workspace and OneLogin.

## Setting up SSO

An owner opens **Admin › Security › Single sign-on**, adds the identity provider's metadata URL
and verifies the email domain (for example `acme.com`) with a DNS TXT record. Users are created
on first sign-in if "Just-in-time provisioning" is on. Enterprise plans also support SCIM.

# Flowdesk FAQ

## I can't sign in. What should I check?

Most sign-in problems have one of a handful of causes. Go through them in order:

1. **The error message.** Every sign-in error has a code (for example `AUTH_423_LOCKED`); see
   [Error codes](error-codes.md) for what each one means.
2. **Too many attempts.** After 5 wrong passwords in 15 minutes the account is locked for
   30 minutes. See [Signing in](sign-in.md#account-lockout).
3. **Your organization uses SSO.** If your admin turned on "Require SSO", the email and password
   form no longer works for you: use **Sign in with SSO**. See [Single sign-on](sso.md).
4. **Two-factor codes.** Codes rejected right after the password usually mean the clock on your
   phone is off. See [Two-factor authentication](two-factor.md#codes-are-rejected).
5. **Your organization's subscription.** If an invoice is unpaid for more than 14 days, the
   workspace is suspended and members can't sign in. See [Billing](billing.md#unpaid-invoices).
6. **An invitation link.** Invitations expire after 7 days. See
   [Members and invitations](members-and-invites.md#invitations).
7. **The desktop app.** Check [Known issues](known-issues.md) for your version.

If none of these fits, contact support with the error code and the time you tried.

passages.label: kb/billing.md › Plans and billing › Unpaid invoices
passages.text:
## Unpaid invoices

If a payment fails, the subscription becomes **past due** and the owner and billing admins are
emailed. Flowdesk retries the card on days 3, 7 and 14.

- During the first **14 days** past due, everything keeps working.
- After 14 days the workspace is **suspended**: members can't sign in and get
  `AUTH_402_ORG_SUSPENDED` ("Your organization's workspace is suspended"). Integrations and the
  API stop too.
- Owners and billing admins can still sign in, but only to **Admin › Billing**, where they can
  pay the open invoice or change the card. Access returns for everyone within a few minutes of a
  successful payment.
- Data of a suspended workspace is kept for **90 days**, then deleted.

Members can't pay on behalf of the organization; they need to contact their owner or billing
admin.

Every error Flowdesk shows has a code. The support form attaches the last one automatically.

| code | message | what it means | what to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

passages.text:
## Creating and managing keys

Admins and owners create keys in **Admin › API keys › New key**, give them a name and choose
scopes (`tasks:read`, `tasks:write`, `projects:read`, `projects:write`, `members:read`). The
full key is shown once; afterwards only its prefix is visible.

A key belongs to the person who created it and acts with their permissions. A key is
**revoked**:

- when someone revokes it in **Admin › API keys**;
- automatically, when the member who created it is **deactivated** or removed from the
  organization;
- when the organization's workspace is suspended (it works again after payment).

A revoked key can't be restored: create a new key and replace it in your integration. To avoid
breakage when people leave, create integration keys from a dedicated service member.

passages.text:
## Passwords

A password needs at least 10 characters. It is checked against lists of leaked passwords;
a rejected password says so. Changing your password signs you out on all other devices.

## Resetting a password

**Forgot password?** on the sign-in page sends a reset link to your email from
`no-reply@flowdesk.app`. The link is valid for **1 hour** and can be used once. If no email
arrives within 10 minutes, check the spam folder, then ask your admin to confirm the email
address on your account.

Resetting your password also **unlocks** an account that was locked after too many attempts.

If your organization requires SSO, there is no Flowdesk password to reset: the reset email
says so and points you to your company's identity provider.

## I forgot my password

Click **Forgot password?** on the sign-in page and enter your email. The reset link arrives from
`no-reply@flowdesk.app` within a few minutes (check spam) and is valid for 1 hour. Resetting the
password also unlocks a locked account.

passages.label: kb/sso.md › Single sign-on (SSO) › Require SSO
passages.text:
## Require SSO

With **Require SSO** on, members of the organization can only sign in through the identity
provider:

- the email and password form rejects them with `AUTH_403_SSO_REQUIRED` ("Your organization
  requires single sign-on");
- **Sign in with Google** is disabled for them;
- password reset emails no longer contain a reset link;
- owners can still sign in with a password, so a broken SSO configuration never locks everyone
  out.

When an admin turns it on, existing sessions stay valid until they expire; the change shows up
the next time someone signs in.

## Account lockout

After **5 failed password attempts within 15 minutes**, the account is locked for
**30 minutes**. While it is locked, every sign-in attempt fails with `AUTH_423_LOCKED`
("Too many attempts. Try again later"), even with the correct password, and does not extend
the lock.

To get back in sooner:

- reset your password with **Forgot password?**: a completed reset unlocks the account at once;
- or ask an admin of your organization to open **Admin › Members**, find you and click
  **Unlock**.

Support can't unlock accounts on the Free and Team plans faster than these two ways.

on first sign-in if "Just-in-time provisioning" is on. Enterprise plans also support SCIM.

# Known issues

Problems we know about, with workarounds. Fixed issues stay listed for 60 days.

## Desktop app for macOS 3.4.0 and 3.4.1: sign-in loop

**Status: fixed in 3.4.2 (released 2026-10-02).**

After signing in through the browser (with Google, SSO or a password), the browser says you are
signed in, but the app shows the sign-in screen again. It happens on macOS 26 because the app
can't save its refresh token in the keychain. The web app is not affected.

Fix: update the app to 3.4.2 or later with **Flowdesk › Check for updates**, or download it from
`flowdesk.app/download`. If the app can't get past the sign-in screen to update, download the
installer from the website and install it over the old version. If the loop continues after
updating, open **Keychain Access**, delete the items named "Flowdesk", and sign in again.

# Flowdesk FAQ

## I can't sign in. What should I check?

Most sign-in problems have one of a handful of causes. Go through them in order:

1. **The error message.** Every sign-in error has a code (for example `AUTH_423_LOCKED`); see
   [Error codes](error-codes.md) for what each one means.
2. **Too many attempts.** After 5 wrong passwords in 15 minutes the account is locked for
   30 minutes. See [Signing in](sign-in.md#account-lockout).
3. **Your organization uses SSO.** If your admin turned on "Require SSO", the email and password
   form no longer works for you: use **Sign in with SSO**. See [Single sign-on](sso.md).
4. **Two-factor codes.** Codes rejected right after the password usually mean the clock on your
   phone is off. See [Two-factor authentication](two-factor.md#codes-are-rejected).
5. **Your organization's subscription.** If an invoice is unpaid for more than 14 days, the
   workspace is suspended and members can't sign in. See [Billing](billing.md#unpaid-invoices).
6. **An invitation link.** Invitations expire after 7 days. See
   [Members and invitations](members-and-invites.md#invitations).
7. **The desktop app.** Check [Known issues](known-issues.md) for your version.

If none of these fits, contact support with the error code and the time you tried.

# Error codes

Every error Flowdesk shows has a code. The support form attaches the last one automatically.

## Sign-in errors

| code | message | what it means | what to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTH_401_BAD_PASSWORD` | Incorrect email or password | the password doesn't match | retype it, or reset it with **Forgot password?** |
| `AUTH_401_OTP_INVALID` | That code didn't work | the two-factor code is wrong or expired | check the device clock, or use a backup code ([Two-factor](two-factor.md#codes-are-rejected)) |
| `AUTH_402_ORG_SUSPENDED` | Your organization's workspace is suspended | the subscription is unpaid for more than 14 days | the owner or a billing admin pays in **Admin › Billing** ([Billing](billing.md#unpaid-invoices)) |
| `AUTH_403_SSO_REQUIRED` | Your organization requires single sign-on | password and Google sign-in are off for this organization | use **Sign in with SSO** ([SSO](sso.md#require-sso)) |
| `AUTH_403_DEACTIVATED` | This account has been deactivated | an admin deactivated the member | ask an admin of the organization |
| `AUTH_423_LOCKED` | Too many attempts. Try again later | 5 failed passwords in 15 minutes locked the account for 30 minutes | wait, reset the password, or ask an admin to unlock ([Lockout](sign-in.md#account-lockout)) |
| `INVITE_EXPIRED` | This invitation has expired | the invitation is older than 7 days | ask an admin to resend it ([Invitations](members-and-invites.md#invitations)) |
| `INVITE_USED` | This invitation was already used | the account exists already | sign in normally |

passages.text:
## Unpaid invoices

If a payment fails, the subscription becomes **past due** and the owner and billing admins are
emailed. Flowdesk retries the card on days 3, 7 and 14.

- During the first **14 days** past due, everything keeps working.
- After 14 days the workspace is **suspended**: members can't sign in and get
  `AUTH_402_ORG_SUSPENDED` ("Your organization's workspace is suspended"). Integrations and the
  API stop too.
- Owners and billing admins can still sign in, but only to **Admin › Billing**, where they can
  pay the open invoice or change the card. Access returns for everyone within a few minutes of a
  successful payment.
- Data of a suspended workspace is kept for **90 days**, then deleted.

Members can't pay on behalf of the organization; they need to contact their owner or billing
admin.

passages.label: kb/two-factor.md › Two-factor authentication › Codes are rejected
passages.text:
## Codes are rejected

A code is valid for 30 seconds and is computed from the current time, so the clock of the
device running the authenticator app matters. If codes fail with `AUTH_401_OTP_INVALID` even
though you type them correctly, the device's clock is almost always off by more than 30 seconds.
This often happens after travelling, when the time zone or time was set by hand.

To fix it:

1. On the phone, turn on automatic date and time (Android: **Settings › System › Date & time ›
   Set time automatically**; iOS: **Settings › General › Date & Time › Set Automatically**).
2. In Google Authenticator on Android you can also use **Settings › Time correction for codes ›
   Sync now**.
3. Wait for a fresh code and try again.

Until the clock is fixed, a **backup code** gets you in.

# API and API keys

The REST API lives at `https://api.flowdesk.app/v2`. It is available on the Team plan and above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an API key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer fd_live_3f9a...
```

Keys start with `fd_live_`. Query parameters (`?api_key=`) are not accepted.

# Error codes

Every error Flowdesk shows has a code. The support form attaches the last one automatically.

## Sign-in errors

| code | message | what it means | what to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTH_401_BAD_PASSWORD` | Incorrect email or password | the password doesn't match | retype it, or reset it with **Forgot password?** |
| `AUTH_401_OTP_INVALID` | That code didn't work | the two-factor code is wrong or expired | check the device clock, or use a backup code ([Two-factor](two-factor.md#codes-are-rejected)) |
| `AUTH_402_ORG_SUSPENDED` | Your organization's workspace is suspended | the subscription is unpaid for more than 14 days | the owner or a billing admin pays in **Admin › Billing** ([Billing](billing.md#unpaid-invoices)) |
| `AUTH_403_SSO_REQUIRED` | Your organization requires single sign-on | password and Google sign-in are off for this organization | use **Sign in with SSO** ([SSO](sso.md#require-sso)) |
| `AUTH_403_DEACTIVATED` | This account has been deactivated | an admin deactivated the member | ask an admin of the organization |
| `AUTH_423_LOCKED` | Too many attempts. Try again later | 5 failed passwords in 15 minutes locked the account for 30 minutes | wait, reset the password, or ask an admin to unlock ([Lockout](sign-in.md#account-lockout)) |
| `INVITE_EXPIRED` | This invitation has expired | the invitation is older than 7 days | ask an admin to resend it ([Invitations](members-and-invites.md#invitations)) |
| `INVITE_USED` | This invitation was already used | the account exists already | sign in normally |

# Export, import and your data

## CSV export

Any project's task list can be exported to CSV from **Project › … › Export › CSV**, with the
current filters applied. One CSV export holds at most **50,000 rows**; a bigger export fails
with `EXPORT_TOO_LARGE`.

- filter the view (for example by date range or status) and export it in parts;
- or, on Business and Enterprise, use the **full workspace export**: **Admin › Data › Export
  workspace**. It contains every project as JSON and CSV files without a row limit, is prepared
  in the background, and a download link (valid 7 days) is emailed to the admin within 24 hours.
- or page through `GET /v2/tasks` in the API.

cases.question: Why did our notifications stop?
cases.answer:
Your notifications may have stopped because the Slack integration is disconnected due to a revoked token, which can happen if the person who connected it left the Slack workspace or if the app was removed [1]. Another possibility is that the mobile app on Android 16 is experiencing delayed notifications if battery optimization is enabled, which can be resolved by disabling it [2]. 

To fix this, check the Slack integration status in **Admin › Integrations** and reconnect if needed. For the mobile app, ensure battery optimization is disabled for Flowdesk.

# Integrations

Integrations are available on the Team plan and above. Admins manage them in
**Admin › Integrations**.

## Slack

Sends task notifications to Slack channels and lets people create tasks with `/flowdesk`.

  **Reconnect**; channel settings are kept.
- Private channels: invite the Flowdesk bot to the channel (`/invite @Flowdesk`) or it can't
  post there.

cases.question: Nobody on my team can sign in. Why?
cases.answer:
If nobody on your team can sign in, it could be due to one of the following reasons:

1. **Your organization's subscription is suspended**. If an invoice is unpaid for more than 14 days, the workspace is suspended, and members can't sign in. This results in the error `AUTH_402_ORG_SUSPENDED` [3]. Owners and billing admins can still sign in to the billing section to resolve the issue.

2. **Members have been deactivated**. If members were deactivated, they will receive the error `AUTH_403_DEACTIVATED` and won't be able to sign in. Admins can reactivate them through the "Members" section, provided there is a free seat available [2].

3. **Your organization requires SSO**. If your organization has "Require SSO" enabled, members can only sign in through the identity provider. The email and password form will reject them with `AUTH_403_SSO_REQUIRED` [4]. Ensure that SSO is properly configured or check with your admin.

4. **Account lockout due to too many failed attempts**. If members have entered incorrect passwords multiple times, their accounts may be locked. This results in the error `AUTH_423_LOCKED` [1].

5. **Invitations have expired**. If members are trying to sign in using an expired invitation link, they will be unable to access the workspace. Invitations expire after 7 days [1].

If none of these apply, contact support with the error code and the time you tried to sign in.

passages.text:
# Flowdesk FAQ

## I can't sign in. What should I check?

Most sign-in problems have one of a handful of causes. Go through them in order:

1. **The error message.** Every sign-in error has a code (for example `AUTH_423_LOCKED`); see
   [Error codes](error-codes.md) for what each one means.
2. **Too many attempts.** After 5 wrong passwords in 15 minutes the account is locked for
   30 minutes. See [Signing in](sign-in.md#account-lockout).
3. **Your organization uses SSO.** If your admin turned on "Require SSO", the email and password
   form no longer works for you: use **Sign in with SSO**. See [Single sign-on](sso.md).
4. **Two-factor codes.** Codes rejected right after the password usually mean the clock on your
   phone is off. See [Two-factor authentication](two-factor.md#codes-are-rejected).
5. **Your organization's subscription.** If an invoice is unpaid for more than 14 days, the
   workspace is suspended and members can't sign in. See [Billing](billing.md#unpaid-invoices).
6. **An invitation link.** Invitations expire after 7 days. See
   [Members and invitations](members-and-invites.md#invitations).
7. **The desktop app.** Check [Known issues](known-issues.md) for your version.

If none of these fits, contact support with the error code and the time you tried.

passages.label: kb/billing.md › Plans and billing › Unpaid invoices
passages.text:
## Unpaid invoices

If a payment fails, the subscription becomes **past due** and the owner and billing admins are
emailed. Flowdesk retries the card on days 3, 7 and 14.

- During the first **14 days** past due, everything keeps working.
- After 14 days the workspace is **suspended**: members can't sign in and get
  `AUTH_402_ORG_SUSPENDED` ("Your organization's workspace is suspended"). Integrations and the
  API stop too.
- Owners and billing admins can still sign in, but only to **Admin › Billing**, where they can
  pay the open invoice or change the card. Access returns for everyone within a few minutes of a
  successful payment.
- Data of a suspended workspace is kept for **90 days**, then deleted.

Members can't pay on behalf of the organization; they need to contact their owner or billing
admin.

passages.label: kb/sign-in.md › Signing in
passages.text:
# Signing in

Flowdesk accepts three ways of signing in: **email and password**, **Sign in with Google**, and
**single sign-on (SSO)** for organizations on the Business and Enterprise plans. Which ones you
can use depends on your organization's settings.

passages.label: kb/sso.md › Single sign-on (SSO) › Require SSO
passages.text:
## Require SSO

With **Require SSO** on, members of the organization can only sign in through the identity
provider:

- the email and password form rejects them with `AUTH_403_SSO_REQUIRED` ("Your organization
  requires single sign-on");
- **Sign in with Google** is disabled for them;
- password reset emails no longer contain a reset link;
- owners can still sign in with a password, so a broken SSO configuration never locks everyone
  out.

When an admin turns it on, existing sessions stay valid until they expire; the change shows up
the next time someone signs in.
